changes.original: Coordinates: alpha=(z-z_prev)/(z_next-z_prev), depth=z/(D-1), gap=(z_next-z_prev)/16.
Normalization: I_norm=2*(clip(I,vmin,vmax)-vmin)/(vmax-vmin+epsilon)-1, with background mapped to -1 and epsilon=1e-7.
Clean latent: z0=0.18215*(mu+sigma*epsilon).
Forward diffusion: z_t=sqrt(alpha_bar_t)*z0+sqrt(1-alpha_bar_t)*epsilon.
Noise objective: E[||epsilon-epsilon_theta(z_t,t,context)||^2].
Deterministic DDIM: predicted z0=(z_t-sqrt(1-alpha_bar_t)*epsilon_theta)/sqrt(alpha_bar_t); z_prev=sqrt(alpha_bar_prev)*predicted z0+sqrt(1-alpha_bar_prev)*epsilon_theta.
VAE objective: L1+0.5*MSE+1e-5*KL+0.1*spatial-gradient L1.
Reconstruction MSE=mean((prediction-target)^2); MAE=mean(abs(prediction-target)); PSNR=10*log10(4/MSE) for [-1,1], with a 100 dB sentinel returned when MSE <= 1e-10.
SSIM uses an 11x11 Gaussian window (sigma 1.5), constants (0.01*2)^2 and (0.03*2)^2, averaged over 2D slices/channels.

Inputs and metadata validator; Hierarchical Data Format version 5 (HDF5, stored as .h5 files) slice reader; acquired-only intensity normalizer; depth/context extractor; weight-tied residual convolutional encoder (base channels 32); three-coordinate Fourier embedding; 17x256 context tokens and 8x30x30 spatial maps; pretrained MedicalAutoencoderKL (4x30x30 latent); conditional U-Net (base channels 64, multipliers 1/2/4); 1000-step noise scheduler; DDIM sampler; batch assembly and optional depth smoothing; Neuroimaging Informatics Technology Initiative (NIfTI)/HDF5 exporter; fidelity metrics and visualization modules. Software runs in Python/PyTorch on CPU or CUDA, with GPU used for the measured experiments.

Input: a registered depth-first stack (D,C,H,W) and unique acquired depth indices including both boundaries. Validate channels, dimensions, finite values and checkpoints. Derive 0.5th/99.5th percentile foreground intensity bounds only from acquired slices; apply the same clipping/scaling to context and targets. For each missing depth locate bounding acquired slices and calculate z/(D-1), alpha and gap/16. Encode context, seed a Gaussian latent, predict noise through 25 or 50 DDIM updates, decode and assign the generated slice. Optionally apply Gaussian smoothing (sigma 0.5 along depth) and restore original acquired values. Export a research NIfTI/HDF5 volume with normalization, seed and checkpoint provenance; evaluate against withheld targets only when available.

Working example: D=155, C=1, H=W=240. At stride 8, acquired indices include 0,8,...,152,154 (21 acquired and 134 missing); at stride 16 they include 0,16,...,144,154 (11 acquired and 144 missing). A target at z=12 bounded by z=8 and z=16 has alpha=0.5, depth=12/154 and normalized gap=0.5. Context is computed only from those acquired slices. The trained VAE maps a 240x240 image to four 30x30 latent channels: 8x spatial downsampling per axis and 16x scalar-element reduction for FLAIR. Code path and results are supplied in sections 15-17.

Audit trail: results/review/test_reference.csv and test_selected.csv contain per-volume metrics; test_reference.json and test_selected.json contain settings and checkpoint identities; experiment_manifest.json, validation_reference.csv, validation_candidate.csv, selection.json, paired_comparison.csv and completion.json record the protocol and selection. Global seed=42; reconstruction seed=42+100*volume_id+stride, e.g. volume 14/stride 8 uses seed 1450. Evaluation uses range [-1,1], missing planes only, 11x11 Gaussian SSIM window sigma=1.5 with zero padding. Generation timing excludes smoothing/metrics, while baseline row timing includes metrics; these values do not support a fair speed-superiority comparison.

Within each volume, PSNR is computed from MSE pooled across all missing-plane pixels; SSIM is averaged across 2D slices/channels. The reported group mean and sample standard deviation summarize the ten per-volume values. DDIM sampling follows the established implicit diffusion formulation (R20), with eta=0 here. The VAE posterior sampling noise and the forward diffusion noise are separate Gaussian draws. Normalization maps intensities <= 1e-7 to background -1; if acquired bounds are degenerate, the implementation uses vmax=vmin+1.

Baseline terminology: smoothed linear interpolation means linear interpolation followed by Gaussian depth smoothing (sigma=0.7). The historical Bspline_3d name is retained only as a compatibility alias; it does not denote a B-spline algorithm.

Local data: 57,195 HDF5 slice files representing 369 volume IDs, each 155 axial planes at 240x240. Each image has four stored channels; current code assumes FLAIR/T1/T1ce/T2 ordering, which requires original HDF5 converter provenance confirmation. Three uint8 mask channels exist; sampled channels are mutually exclusive, so WT/TC/ET semantics are not assumed. Original BraTS is multi-institutional brain-tumor MRI with expert annotations (R6). Patient-volume split uses seed 42: 258 train, 55 validation, 56 test. These are internal partitions of the local training collection, not official challenge test data. Diffusion trains only on missing target planes. Fine-tuning uses equal-probability strides 4/8/16 and acquired-only intensity statistics; VAE stays frozen and encoder/U-Net receive MSE noise-prediction updates with AdamW and gradient clipping. Five fixed validation volumes select settings; ten held-out volumes provide final comparisons. The review experiments use the local collection; no independent clinical study was supplied. Earlier checkpoint/data provenance remains unverified. Fine-tuning completed 3000 training iterations (24000 sampled slice examples with replacement) in 18.49 minutes, stopping at the configured step cap within the 70-minute limit. The candidate did not satisfy the validation improvement criterion, so the corrected original checkpoint remains selected.
